sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Competitive Gaming Matchmaking and Tournament Systems

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: federal common-law constitutional framework over the civil-law private law of Quebec governed by the Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c CCQ-1991), with a French-language statutory overlay for commercial legal publicity
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada–China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA), in force October 1, 2014
Canada–EU Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), provisionally applied since 2017
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada's network of 90+ double taxation avoidance agreements (DTAAs) with the OECD Multilateral Instrument overlay

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec (CQLR c CCQ-1991), arts. 2236-2246 (limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), arts. 1-111; Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11) for LP designation rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar), under the Ministère de la Justice du Québec; online services at servicesenligne.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership (Déclaration d'immatriculation - société en commandite), filed under art. 2236 C.C.Q. and art. 12 et seq. of the ALPE
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No mandatory paid-up capital. Under art. 2245 C.C.Q., a limited partner's liability shield requires an actual contribution to the partnership fund, but no minimum amount, escrow account, or notarized capital statement is imposed by the ALPE.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE GENERAL PARTNER - SUBSCRIPTIONS, HEAD OFFICE AND OFFICERS. The undersigned General Partner of [LP name], Limited Partnership, acting as the Partnership's sole governing body, hereby resolves: (1) the General Partner's and each Limited Partner's capital subscription, as set out in the Contribution Schedule, is accepted; (2) the Partnership's head office is established at [address, Montreal, Quebec]; (3) [full name] is appointed Manager and authorized signatory with full authority to open bank accounts and execute commercial contracts; (4) the Manager is instructed to file the Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and complete all required tax, municipal and regulatory filings; (5) this resolution takes effect immediately. Adopted this [date] at Montréal, Québec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: LP Name Availability Search and French-Language Compliance Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - online name-search service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify via the REQ registration database that the proposed designation is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing enterprise name and complies with the Charter of the French Language (the name must have a French form and a proper ending such as 'S.E.C.' or 'L.P.'). Submit an optional name-reservation request; a reservation holds the name for 120 days.
required_dossiers: Proposed designation with corporate ending (S.E.C./L.P.)
Principal activities description (competitive gaming matchmaking and tournament platform)
Request for name search certificate (demande d'attestation de recherche de nom)
Contact details of the applicant general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ refuses the designation as non-distinctive or non-compliant, the filer may (i) amend the designation with additional distinguishing elements and re-submit, (ii) obtain written consent from the earlier name holder, or (iii) apply to the Court of Québec for a designation review within 60 days of the refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Electronic Filing of the Declaration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec - online filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the official Déclaration d'immatriculation (société en commandite) form identifying each general and limited partner, head office address, place where partnership books and records are kept, and the general partner's residential address. Sign the declaration electronically with the authorized representative's credential and pay the CAD $35 filing fee. Upon approval, the REQ issues the Certificate of Registration and the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ); partnership registers must then be opened at the head office.
required_dossiers: Completed declaration form (partner identities, addresses, contributions)
Name search certificate or reservation receipt (if obtained)
Proof of head-office address in Quebec (e.g., commercial lease)
Copy of the limited partnership agreement (kept with registers; not filed)
Electronic signature credential (clé d'accès) or mandate of the authorized representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the declaration is queried for incompleteness (e.g., missing partner address or non-French name), the REQ sends a notice of incompleteness; the filer corrects the declaration within the indicated deadline. A formal refusal may be cured by re-filing with full disclosure or contested by judicial review before the Superior Court of Quebec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registrations - GST/HST, QST, Payroll and QPIP
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec - Mon dossier entreprise (business registration portal); Canada Revenue Agency under the federal-provincial tax administration agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the NEQ, open the GST/HST account, the Quebec Sales Tax (TVQ) account, the source-deductions employer account, and the Quebec Parental Insurance Plan (QPIP) account. Revenu Québec provides one-stop registration for Quebec-based businesses. If the Partnership employs staff, register the employer classification with the CNESST for mandatory workplace insurance coverage.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration (NEQ attestation)
Partnership agreement (for pass-through tax characterization)
Social insurance / business numbers of the general partner and manager
Bank confirmation of commercial account
Projected taxable revenues and payroll estimate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Revenu Québec requests additional information, file a written response with corrected data; any notice of assessment or refusal may be objected to within 90 days under the Taxation Act (CQLR c I-3) before the Court of Québec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Building/Fire Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ville de Montréal - Service des permis d'affaires (or municipal permit office of the relevant Quebec municipality); municipal fire prevention service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For physical offices or tournament venues, apply for a commercial occupation permit (permis d'affaires / permis d'occupation) and obtain a certificate of compliance from the fire prevention service (visa de sécurité incendie). Provide a floor plan with occupant load and exits, a licensed engineer/architect certificate for structural load where spectator seating is installed, and accessibility compliance under the Quebec Construction Code. Electronic-only platforms without premises may skip this step.
required_dossiers: Municipal licence application form
Proof of occupation (lease or deed)
Floor plan and maximum occupant load calculation
Fire safety inspection report / certificate
Engineer/architect certificate for structural loads (if public venue)
REQ and Revenu Québec registration attestations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal permit is refused, request an administrative review by the borough council committee; unresolved refusals may be challenged before the Superior Court of Quebec. Fire-safety non-compliance is cured by submitting and executing a corrective action plan approved by the municipal fire marshal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Annual Declarations, Amendments and Employer Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec; Revenu Québec; CNESST
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the annual declaration with the REQ within 60 days of each registration anniversary and pay the graduated annual fee. Declare any change of head office, general partner, or contributed capital within 15 days of the change. File the partnership information returns (federal T5013 and Quebec TP-600), issue partner allocation slips as prescribed by Revenu Québec, and file GST/QST returns according to the assigned cycle. Register as an employer with CNESST and post workplace safety notices; prize-payout withholding analysis is required before disbursing esports tournament winnings.
required_dossiers: Annual declaration data (current partner list, addresses)
Updated partnership agreement and capital account ledger
T5013/TP-600 return data package
Payroll records and CNESST classification code
Prize-payout withholding policy for tournament winnings
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late annual declarations trigger an ALPE late-filing penalty; pay the arrears and file within the cure window to stop accrual. A contested administrative penalty may be referred to the Tribunal administratif du Québec or the Court of Québec depending on the quantum.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board applies to a software/esports platform. General business oversight: Registraire des entreprises du Québec and Revenu Québec; premises matters: municipal permit services. If real-money or casino-type tournament games are offered, the Régie des alcools, des courses et des jeux (RACJ) would assume licensing jurisdiction.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No provincial sectoral operating licence is required for ISIC 5820. Municipal business licence (permis d'affaires) and occupancy permit apply only where physical premises are used; conditional RACJ gaming licence applies only if the platform operates real-money betting or games of chance.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - pure software/service platform; no listed industrial activity under Schedule A of the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment and review (CQLR c Q-2, r. 23); no ministerial EIA report required for administrative offices or tournament operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No fixed industrial discharge thresholds apply to a software platform. If on-site standby generators or data halls are installed, the Clean Air Regulation (CQLR c Q-2, r. 4.1) VOC/GHG standards and municipal noise bylaws apply; effluent to municipal sewer must meet municipal sewer-use standards; electronic waste must be routed to a compliant recovery program under the Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of products by enterprises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal fire safety clearance (visa de sécurité incendie) and occupancy permit under the Quebec Construction Code and Safety Code; structural load review by a licensed engineer where spectator/tournament seating is installed; CNESST registration, first-aid equipment, and a written workplace health-and-safety program for employees; accessibility compliance for public venues under the Act to secure handicapped persons in the exercise of their rights.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — canada.ca — for federal GST/HST and federal income tax; Revenu Québec — revenuquebec.ca — for Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and Quebec provincial income tax. CRA applies the federal Excise Tax Act and the Income Tax Act; Revenu Québec applies the Tax Administration Act (Quebec) and the Taxation Act (Quebec).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign limited partnership must obtain a CRA Business Number (BN) through Business Registration Online (BRO) or written Form RC1. It then registers for a federal GST/HST account once taxable supplies made in Canada exceed the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold measured over four consecutive calendar quarters. For Quebec, the LP must file Form RQ-0001 with Revenu Québec to obtain a QST registration number and a provincial-qualification business number. The LP files a T5013 partnership information return identifying all partners, including non-resident partners; a Canadian resident representative or agent should be designated for service of process and filings. Quebec payroll and health-services-fund accounts are also required if the LP employs Canadian staff.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. The Quebec limited partnership is fiscally transparent: it is not a taxpayer under the federal Income Tax Act or the Quebec Taxation Act. Each partner reports its allocable share of partnership income or loss. Non-resident partners carrying on business in Canada through the LP are taxable under Part I of the Income Tax Act on their share of Canadian-source partnership business income; separate Canadian-source amounts (such as management fees, royalties, or certain investment returns) may be subject to Part XIII withholding, subject to applicable tax treaty relief.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box election; LP pass-through treatment is mandatory, not elective. For GST/HST and QST purposes, the partnership itself registers and accounts as a registrant in the partnership name. Applicable elections and mechanisms include the hybrid-mismatch rules under Part I of the Income Tax Act (effective 1 July 2022 per BEPS Action 2) which may disallow deductions for payments subject to inconsistent tax treatment in the foreign partner's residence jurisdiction; partnership income-allocation agreements that reflect the partners' true economic interests under section 96 of the Income Tax Act; and the election to treat the partnership as a separate person for certain foreign-accrual and offshore-fund computations under subsection 96(3).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) combined with Quebec Sales Tax (QST); Quebec does not apply the Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) single-rate model.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies made in Canada over four consecutive calendar quarters; the QST threshold in Quebec is identically CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies. Esports platform subscriptions, tournament entry fees, and digital matchmaking services are taxable supplies of digital services, so mandatory registration is triggered once the threshold is exceeded. Registration is also required earlier where the LP voluntarily registers or carries on a commercial activity in Quebec through a permanent establishment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec impose no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, no digital stamping, and no government API clearance regime for e-commerce or software platforms. Electronic invoices and payment records, including Stripe and PayPal settlement files, are accepted for audit purposes if they meet CRA's Books and Records Requirements and Revenu Québec's record-keeping rules. Every invoice issued by a Quebec enterprise must be drawn up in French or accompanied by an approved French version and must show the GST/HST registration number, the QST registration number, the rates applied, and, for zero-rated exports, the statutory basis of the zero-rating.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for (i) goods exported by the vendor pursuant to Schedule VI of the Excise Tax Act, and (ii) digital services and intangible personal property supplied to a non-resident recipient under Schedule VI, Part V, provided the supply is not in respect of real property situated in Canada and not in respect of tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed, and provided the recipient is a non-resident not registered for GST/QST. An esports community platform charging entry fees, subscriptions, and tournament platform fees to foreign users may zero-rate those supplies where the service is enjoyed wholly outside Canada; QST zero-rating mirrors the GST treatment under Quebec rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Border Services Agency Form B13 or EDI electronic equivalent)
Commercial invoice and detailed packing list
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export movement
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 evidencing foreign-currency settlement
Signed platform terms or contract confirming the recipient's non-resident status and the offshore place of enjoyment
Zero-rated invoice, compliant with Quebec French-language rules, bearing the LP's GST/HST and QST registration numbers
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess within the normal four-year limitation period, and without limitation where misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud is established. If export zero-rating is denied, the LP becomes liable for the uncollected GST/QST together with arrears interest calculated at the prescribed CRA/Revenu Québec rates. Statutory penalties include a minimum penalty of CAD 250 or 25% of the net tax understated for knowingly false statements, rising to 50% for gross negligence and on repeat offences; criminal prosecution for wilful evasion or intentional filing of false returns is available under the offences provisions of the Excise Tax Act and the Québec Tax Administration Act, carrying substantial fines and imprisonment of up to five years on summary conviction.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) and Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); foreign exchange administration is also subject to the regulatory oversight of FINTRAC and the Department of Finance Canada for sanctions and cross-border reporting
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full convertibility of the Canadian dollar on both current and capital account. There are no exchange control restrictions on profit repatriation, dividend distributions, loan repayments, or capital contributions, subject to corporate law solvency tests, tax compliance, and anti-money-laundering reporting. Non-resident partners of a Quebec limited partnership may repatriate distributable profits in any freely convertible currency, provided that the LP complies with Part VII of the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and, where applicable, the Special Economic Measures Act sanctions regime. Payments in excess of C$10,000 crossing the Canadian border must be reported to the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no export proceeds surrender requirements in Canada. Exporters and service providers such as the esports platform may retain all export receipts in the currency of invoicing, convert freely at commercial bank rates, or deploy them for treasury purposes. The Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) may require full reporting of foreign revenue for income tax; the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) requires reporting of large cross-border wire transfers of C$10,000 or more. No mandatory conversion ratio or statutory timeline applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium feasibility for purely offshore electronic money institutions (EMIs) other than Canadian chartered banks. A foreign EMI may not hold or operate as a full banking entity in Canada without a federal or provincial banking licence; however, it may provide payment processing services on a software-as-a-service basis if it registers with the Bank of Canada under the Retail Payment Activities Act and complies with FINTRAC as a foreign money services business. For direct treasury clearing and high-volume tournament payouts, a tier-1 Canadian bank account remains necessary; integration with Stripe and PayPal should be made through the bank's merchant acquiring and payout gateway.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required. For a limited partnership opening a corporate account with a tier-1 Canadian bank, the general partner's director, the investment manager, or the authorized financial signatory must attend an in-person KYC interview at a bank branch in Canada, or satisfy an approved video-identification process if the bank permits remote onboarding for corporate accounts. In practice, most major Canadian banks require physical appearance of at least one senior officer and direct identification of all significant beneficial owners. Remote opening is rarely permitted for non-resident partnerships; a notarized or apostilled resolution and passport copies are mandatory but not sufficient alone.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident general partner or beneficial owner without a Canadian address
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified general partner registry extract from the home jurisdiction, apostilled, notarized LP agreement evidencing ownership and control, signed KYC attestation, beneficial ownership schedule identifying all natural persons owning 25% or more, and a Canadian registered agent address for service.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume non-face-to-face esports microtransactions flagged as unusual payment activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved AML/CFT compliance manual, business plan describing tournament payout mechanics, history of platform contractual terms, player verification policy, anti-fraud and transaction monitoring system reports, and a projected transaction profile with segregated tournament pool accounting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of initial capital contribution from cross-border cryptocurrency conversion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cryptocurrency exchange audited transaction history, wallet-associated KYC records, exchange withdrawal confirmation matching the capital contribution amount and date, sworn source-of-funds affidavit, and professional accounting reconciliation of the capital escrow ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Director or beneficial owner appearing on a sanctions or politically exposed persons (PEP) watchlist
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent global sanctions screening conducted by a licensed compliance provider within 24 hours, with negative match results from OSFI, Global Affairs Canada, OFAC, EU, UN and consolidated PEP databases, explained declarations of identity, and a bank-compliant enhanced due diligence questionnaire.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions from non-resident limited partners are routed by international SWIFT MT103 wire to the LP's tier-1 operational or capital escrow account in Montreal or Toronto. The remittance instruction must quote the Canadian recipient bank's SWIFT BIC, the LP's Canadian bank account number and institution/transit codes, and a purpose-of-payment code such as 'Capital contribution to Limited Partnership (TREA)' or 'Intercompany treasury funding' with cross-reference to the LP agreement. Verification includes submission of the executed capital call notice, LP agreement, confirmation of the transferor's bank identity, and FINTRAC large transaction reporting if C$10,000 or more in a single or linked transaction. No foreign exchange restriction applies to the conversion of USD to CAD; conversion occurs at the bank's spot rate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for tournament prize pools, platform service fees, and cross-border partner disbursements clear via (i) SWIFT MT103 corporate-to-corporate wires for international payouts; (ii) commercial letters of credit (LC) issued under UCP600 vendor-payment terms for contractual trade obligations; (iii) Payments Canada Large-Value Transfer System (LVTS) / Lynx for high-value Canadian-dollar settlements; and (iv) standard Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) rails for domestic ACH-style payments. Stripe and PayPal integration operate as merchant acquiring rails feeding net proceeds to the operational account with daily sweeps.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign exchange forwards in USD/CAD and EUR/CAD for contracted tournament revenue
Foreign exchange swaps for scheduled capital injections and dividend distributions
Cross-currency basis swaps for long-term non-resident partner capital account hedges
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for currencies with no deliverable domestic forward market, permitted for hedging not speculation
Futures contracts on CME for Canadian dollar and US dollar crosses, subject to exchange and clearing membership requirements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Registrar of Enterprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary date of the initial registration each year (e.g., an enterprise registered on March 15 must file the annual declaration by March 15 of each subsequent year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of approximately CAD 57.75; if the declaration remains unfiled after a formal default notice, the registraire may administratively strike off (radier) the enterprise registration after a further notice period. Substantial repeated delinquency triggers cancellation of the partnership's registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (annual federal partnership income and allocation filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the partnership's fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, due on or before May 31 of the following calendar year. Penalty applies if the return is received after the due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per partner per day (minimum CAD 125 and maximum CAD 2,500) for the regulating general partner; CRA may also reassess the partnership's income if the T5013 is not filed.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory independent audit is required for an ordinary private Quebec limited partnership, unless the partnership is a reporting issuer under the Quebec Securities Act, is a regulated investment fund, or the partnership agreement expressly requires an annual audit. Certain government contracts or financial covenants may also trigger an audit obligation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, CPA Canada Handbook Part II) for private limited partnerships; International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS, Part I) if the partnership is a publicly accountable entity or has elected IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no separate annual UBO declaration for Quebec limited partnerships. The Registraire des entreprises annual declaration confirms the identity and address of each general partner; any announced change in partners, contributions, or general partnership roles must be filed through an amendment to the registration file. Beneficial ownership transparency is achieved through the maintained partner register and the partnership agreement rather than a distinct annual UBO filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (including contributions and profit share)
Register of General Partners (including residential or professional addresses)
Minute Book of Partners' Meetings and Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $100 - $300 per year (typical registered office service in Quebec)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required internally; if an audit is triggered, $4,000 - $12,000 depending on asset size and transaction volume.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined general corporate income tax rate in Quebec, comprising 11.5% federal general rate plus 11.5% Quebec provincial rate (both effective 2023 onward; federal rate reduced where taxable income is allocated to a province and subject to the Quebec abatement).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal small business deduction: 9% federal rate on first CAD 500,000 of active business income per associated group; Quebec small business deduction: 3.2% provincial rate on first CAD 500,000 of active business income per associated group, resulting in an approximately 12.2% combined rate for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations; not applicable to a Limited Partnership used as a pass-through vehicle, but available to corporate partners holding LP interests. No general Quebec tax holiday for esports platform operators; limited refundable tax credits for multimedia (Quebec Multimedia Tax Credit) may apply if the platform produces eligible multimedia content tied to Quebec labour costs. The LP itself computes income at the partner level; no standalone corporate income tax holiday.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Limited Partnership: not a separate taxpayer for income tax; partners file their share of LP income via their own returns. The partnership must file an information return through Revenu Québec, notably the Revenu Québec RL-15 slip and the federal T5013 Partnership Information Return (if the LP has Canadian-resident partners or carries on business in Canada), via the CRA My Business Account portal and Revenu Québec’s Mon dossier d’entreprise portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T5013: due no later than March 31 of the following calendar year for a December 31 year-end, extended to May 1 where the partnership is required to file electronically and all partners are individuals; RL-15: due no later than February 28 of the following calendar year; Quebec corporate partners must include the LP allocation in their corporate T2/CO-17 returns due six months after each corporate fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Limited partner’s share of business income (loss) at the federal level from the partnership’s active business operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners report only Canadian-source partnership income; the T5013 is filed by the partnership (or its designated representative), not the non-resident partner. Withhold or report Part XIII tax on passive allocations as applicable; active business allocations may require a Part I return by the non-resident partner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership’s total revenues and total expenses from the esports platform operations; boxes used by the LP to reconcile net business income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners should obtain the T5013 allocation but are generally not required to file annually solely for the allocation unless they carry on business in Canada through the LP; the LP must withhold on any management fees or other Part XIII amounts paid to non-residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Québec allocation of the partnership’s business income (loss) and investment income (loss) of each Québec-resident or non-resident partner carrying on business in Québec.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The LP must issue RL-15 slips for each partner, including non-residents with Québec-source income. Non-resident partners may be required to file a Quebec income return to report Québec-source business income; the RL-15 is an information slip and does not satisfy the partner’s filing obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year capital cost allowance (depreciation) claimed by the partnership on servers, software, hardware, and platform intangibles.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners need the information to compute their own depreciation recapture or capital gains on disposition; the LP claims CCA at entity level and allocates net income after CCA to partners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interests paid or payable by the partnership to partners or third parties on capital contributions; relevant for withholding obligations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid by an LP to a non-resident lender is subject to Part XIII withholding tax at 25% unless reduced under the Canada-U.S. or Canada-other treaty; the LP must file NR4 returns and remit withholding.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of T5013: CAD 25–100 per day for each partner, up to 12 months, minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 7,500 for partnerships with 1–250 partners (increased for larger partnerships); late filing of RL-15: CAD 25 per day per slip, minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 25,000; additional penalties for repeat non-compliance and for failure to file information returns in prescribed electronic format; failure to remit non-resident withholding tax: 10% late penalty plus daily interest at the prescribed CRA/Revenu Québec rate (currently approximately 5% for CRA, plus Revenu Québec’s rate of about 6% for corporate accounts).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on dividends remitted by a Canadian-resident corporation to a non-resident shareholder under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act; not applicable to the LP itself, but applies when a corporate partner distributes profits to foreign investors.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit a Canada Revenue Agency NR301 (or applicable treaty-specific form) declaration, provide a valid Certificate of Residence (Form 6166 for U.S. residents, or equivalent forms for other treaty jurisdictions) to the Canadian payer before the payment date, and the payer must withhold the reduced treaty rate or request a refund under the reciprocal treaty process. Quebec follows the federal treaty allocation rules via the Taxation Act; the RL-15/T5013 allocation determines source. Reduced rates commonly: U.S.-Canada treaty dividends generally 15% (5% for significant shareholdings), royalties 0% (arm’s length) or 10% (non-arm’s length), interest 0% or 10% subject to limitations.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: royalties 25%, interest 25% on cross-border payments to non-residents; treaty rates under Canada-U.S. treaty: arm’s length royalties 0%, non-arm’s length 10%; interest frequently 0% for arm’s length, 10% for non-arm’s length; Canada-Quebec does not add a separate provincial withholding tax beyond the federal Part XIII.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Canadian transfer-pricing documentation (Local File/Master File under CRA’s administrative guidance) is required where the transaction value exceeds CAD 5 million (gross revenues for the year) or the aggregate value of controlled transactions exceeds CAD 5 million for a taxation year. Quebec does not impose a separate TP documentation threshold but adopts federal TP rules under the Taxation Act.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) do not apply in Canada in the form used in the UAE or other Gulf jurisdictions. Canada instead applies statutory General Anti-Avoidance Rules (GAAR) and the specified partnership/limited partnership ‘business limit’ restrictions, which require genuine activity, real risk-bearing partners, and commercial purpose. If the LP is a Manitoba-qualified limited partnership under Quebec law, its limited partners lose limited liability if they take part in control of the business; for tax purposes, all partners must reflect economic substance of the platform operations, and CRA may recharacterize allocations without real economic risk as nothing more than profit-sharing arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Mischaracterization of partnership income and non-resident allocations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring the LP so that substantially all Canadian-source service revenue is allocated to non-resident partners who provide no services and bear no meaningful economic risk; using the LP as a pure invoice conduit with minimal Canadian substance; failing to report the partnership’s Canadian business income via T5013/RL-15.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may reassess the allocation under GAAR, impute income to the Canadian partners, disallow expenses, and impose a 10% gross-negligence penalty on amounts misreported; Revenu Québec may similarly reassess under the Taxation Act, with penalties up to CAD 5,000 for non-filing or false statements, plus daily interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner can be held personally liable for unremitted withholding taxes and the corporation’s unpaid tax liabilities under ITA s.227.1; willful participation in a partnership-veil tax scheme may lead to civil restitution and exclusion from future CRA compliance programs; criminal tax evasion carries imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to withhold Part XIII tax on royalties/interest/dividends paid to non-residents
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying platform licensing royalties, interest on shareholder loans, or service fees to U.S./offshore related parties without making the required 25% withholding or without filing NR4 returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Liability for the full unreported 25% withholding tax, interest on arrears, a 10% late-remittance penalty, and penalties for failure to file NR4 information returns; Revenu Québec may separately assess provincial penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the general-partner corporation are jointly and severally liable for the unremitted tax under ITA s.227.1; gross negligence or deliberate non-withholding exposes board members to significant personal enforcement and CRA’s director-liability procedures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing non-arm’s length services and intangibles
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging below-market royalty or management fees to a foreign esports-platform affiliate, transferring user data or platform goodwill to a low-tax jurisdiction, or inflating charges from offshore service providers without functional analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may adjust transfer pricing under s.247(2), impose transfer-pricing penalties of 10% of net adjustment (minimum CAD 5,000) when the adjustment exceeds the threshold and the taxpayer fails to make reasonable efforts; 5% GAAR penalty possible; reassessments are not statute-barred where misrepresentation is proven.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Transfer-pricing penalty assessed on the partnership or corporate partner is normally not automatically recoverable from directors absent gross negligence or deliberate avoidance; willful participation can trigger criminal liability under the Income Tax Act or Criminal Code for tax evasion, including imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failing to file T5013/RL-15 and income tax returns for the LPs
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Continuously operating the Quebec esports platform partnership for more than a full fiscal year without filing the partnership information returns, allocating no income to resident partners, and failing to register for the QST/QST/HST on tournament fees and platform subscriptions cross-border.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Minimum CAD 100 and daily penalties up to CAD 7,500 (T5013), CAD 25,000 (RL-15), federal/Quebec interest, and the potential loss of the right to claim business expenses; if the LP is later deemed to be a corporation for tax purposes under the Canadian anti-hybrid rules, exposure increases to corporate income tax rates plus penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner who authored the repeated omissions are personally liable under federal and Quebec tax laws for the amounts owing; civil travel bans may issue for significant outstanding tax liabilities; evidence of deliberate concealment supports fraud prosecution and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Banking red flags on tournament payout flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the LP bank account to receive player entry fees and immediately payout tournament prizes without recording beneficial ownership, without client due diligence, or through payment processors (Stripe/PayPal) that report high-volume chargebacks or unexplained cross-border flows to FINTRAC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FINTRAC administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1 million per violation for money-services-business failures; banks may freeze accounts under Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act; tax authorities can treat unreported prize fees as unreported income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers of the general-partner corporation may be subject to personal FINTRAC penalties only where they directed the violations; criminal money-laundering charges can include up to 10 years’ imprisonment and asset forfeiture.
